sanskrit: manasvī balavāñ śūraḥ kṛtāstro dṛḍhavikramaḥ dūrapātī dṛḍheṣuś ca nimittajñaś ca pāṇḍavaḥ
english: High-spirited, strong, and valiant, master of his weapons and firm in prowess, striking from afar with unerring shafts, and reading the omens well — such is the son of Pāṇḍu.

sanskrit: ajeyaḥ samare caiva devair api savāsavaiḥ balavān buddhimāṃś caiva jitakleśo yudhāṃ varaḥ
english: Unconquerable in battle even by the gods with Vāsava at their head, mighty and wise, having mastered all hardship, he is the foremost of warriors.

sanskrit: vijayī ca raṇe nityaṃ bhairavāstraś ca pāṇḍavaḥ tasya mārgaṃ pariharan drutaṃ gaccha yatavratam
english: Ever victorious in war and wielder of terrible weapons is this son of Pāṇḍu. Avoiding his path, go swiftly, you whose vows are firm.

sanskrit: paśya caitan mahābāho vaiśasaṃ samupasthitam hemacitrāṇi śūrāṇāṃ mahānti ca śubhāni ca
english: Behold, O mighty-armed one, the carnage that has drawn near — the great and splendid armor of heroes, wrought with gold,

sanskrit: kavacāny avadīryante śaraiḥ saṃnataparvabhiḥ chidyante ca dhvajāgrāṇi tomarāṇi dhanūṃṣi ca
english: these coats of mail are being shattered by arrows with their well-jointed shafts, and the tips of banners, the lances, and the bows are being cut to pieces,

sanskrit: prāsāś ca vimalās tīkṣṇāḥ śaktyaś ca kanakojjvalāḥ vaijayantyaś ca nāgānāṃ saṃkruddhena kirīṭinā
english: and the bright keen spears, the gold-gleaming javelins, and the pennons of the elephants — all by the wrath of the Diademed One.

sanskrit: nāyaṃ saṃrakṣituṃ kālaḥ prāṇān putropajīvibhiḥ yāhi svargaṃ puraskṛtya yaśase vijayāya ca
english: This is no time for those who live for their sons to guard their lives. Go forth, setting heaven before you, for glory and for victory.

sanskrit: hayanāgarathāvartāṃ mahāghorāṃ sudustarām rathena saṃgrāmanadīṃ taraty eṣa kapidhvajaḥ
english: This warrior whose banner bears the ape crosses in his chariot the river of battle — most dreadful and hard to ford, its whirlpools the steeds, the elephants, and the cars.

sanskrit: brahmaṇyatā damo dānaṃ tapaś ca caritaṃ mahat ihaiva dṛśyate rājño bhrātā yasya dhanaṃjayaḥ
english: Devotion to the brāhmaṇas, self-restraint, generosity, and great austerity practiced — all this is seen here in the king whose brother is Dhanaṃjaya.

sanskrit: bhīmasenaś ca balavān mādrīputrau ca pāṇḍavau vāsudevaś ca vārṣṇeyo yasya nātho vyavasthitaḥ
english: Mighty Bhīmasena, the two sons of Mādrī, and Vāsudeva of the Vṛṣṇis — these stand as his protectors.

sanskrit: tasyaiṣa manyuprabhavo dhārtarāṣṭrasya durmateḥ tapodagdhaśarīrasya kopo dahati bhāratān
english: Born of his wrath against the evil-minded son of Dhṛtarāṣṭra, the anger of that king, his body seared by penance, now consumes the Bhāratas.

sanskrit: eṣa saṃdṛśyate pārtho vāsudevavyapāśrayaḥ dārayan sarvasainyāni dhārtarāṣṭrāṇi sarvaśaḥ
english: There Pārtha is seen, with Vāsudeva for his refuge, rending utterly all the armies of Dhṛtarāṣṭra's son on every side.

sanskrit: etad ālokyate sainyaṃ kṣobhyamāṇaṃ kirīṭinā mahorminaddhaṃ sumahat timineva nadīmukham
english: Behold this host being thrown into turmoil by the Diademed One, like the vast mouth of a river bound up with great waves and churned by a leviathan.

sanskrit: hāhākilakilāśabdāḥ śrūyante ca camūmukhe yāhi pāñcāladāyādam ahaṃ yāsye yudhiṣṭhiram
english: Cries of woe and shrieks of dismay are heard at the front of the army. Go you against the heir of the Pāñcālas; I shall go against Yudhiṣṭhira.

sanskrit: durlabhaṃ hy antaraṃ rājño vyūhasyāmitatejasaḥ samudrakukṣipratimaṃ sarvato 'tirathaiḥ sthitaiḥ
english: Hard indeed to find is an opening to the king's battle-array of boundless splendor — like the belly of the ocean, hemmed in on every side by mighty car-warriors who stand their ground.

sanskrit: sātyakiś cābhimanyuś ca dhṛṣṭadyumnavṛkodarau parirakṣanti rājānaṃ yamau ca manujeśvaram
english: Sātyaki and Abhimanyu, Dhṛṣṭadyumna and Vṛkodara, and the twins guard the king, that lord of men, on every side.

sanskrit: upendrasadṛśaḥ śyāmo mahāśāla ivodgataḥ eṣa gacchaty anīkāni dvitīya iva phalgunaḥ
english: Dark like Upendra, towering like a great sāla tree risen up, this one advances against the ranks like a second Phalguna.

sanskrit: uttamāstrāṇi cādatsva gṛhītvānyan mahad dhanuḥ pārśvato yāhi rājānaṃ yudhyasva ca vṛkodaram
english: Take up your finest weapons, and grasping another great bow, advance to the king's flank and do battle with Vṛkodara.

sanskrit: ko hi necchet priyaṃ putraṃ jīvantaṃ śāśvatīḥ samāḥ kṣatradharmaṃ puraskṛtya tatas tvā viniyujmahe
english: For who would not wish his beloved son to live through endless years? Yet setting the duty of a kṣatriya foremost, I therefore appoint you to this task.

sanskrit: eṣa cāpi raṇe bhīṣmo dahate vai mahācamūm yuddhe susadṛśas tāta yamasya varuṇasya ca
english: And there too Bhīṣma in battle consumes the great host — in combat, dear son, the very peer of Yama and of Varuṇa.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca bhagadattaḥ kṛpaḥ śalyaḥ kṛtavarmā ca sātvataḥ vindānuvindāv āvantyau saindhavaś ca jayadrathaḥ
english: Saṃjaya said: Bhagadatta, Kṛpa, Śalya, and Kṛtavarman of the Sātvatas, Vinda and Anuvinda of Avanti, and Jayadratha the lord of the Sindhus —

sanskrit: citraseno vikarṇaś ca tathā durmarṣaṇo yuvā daśaite tāvakā yodhā bhīmasenam ayodhayan
english: Citrasena and Vikarṇa, and the youthful Durmarṣaṇa — these ten warriors of your side gave battle to Bhīmasena.

sanskrit: mahatyā senayā yuktā nānādeśasamutthayā bhīṣmasya samare rājan prārthayānā mahad yaśaḥ
english: Joined with a mighty host gathered from many lands, O king, they sought in the battle great renown for Bhīṣma's sake.

sanskrit: śalyas tu navabhir bāṇair bhīmasenam atāḍayat kṛtavarmā tribhir bāṇaiḥ kṛpaś ca navabhiḥ śaraiḥ
english: Śalya then struck Bhīmasena with nine arrows, Kṛtavarman with three, and Kṛpa with nine shafts.

sanskrit: citraseno vikarṇaś ca bhagadattaś ca māriṣa daśabhir daśabhir bhallair bhīmasenam atāḍayan
english: Citrasena, Vikarṇa, and Bhagadatta, O venerable one, each struck Bhīmasena with ten broad-headed shafts.

sanskrit: saindhavaś ca tribhir bāṇair jatrudeśe 'bhyatāḍayat vindānuvindāv āvantyau pañcabhiḥ pañcabhiḥ śaraiḥ durmarṣaṇaś ca viṃśatyā pāṇḍavaṃ niśitaiḥ śaraiḥ
english: And the lord of the Sindhus struck him with three arrows upon the collarbone; Vinda and Anuvinda of Avanti with five shafts each; and Durmarṣaṇa pierced the son of Pāṇḍu with twenty sharpened arrows.

sanskrit: sa tān sarvān mahārāja bhrājamānān pṛthak pṛthak pravīrān sarvalokasya dhārtarāṣṭrān mahārathān vivyādha bahubhir bāṇair bhīmaseno mahābalaḥ
english: Then, O great king, the mighty Bhīmasena pierced them all with many arrows — those resplendent heroes, the great car-warriors of Dhṛtarāṣṭra's party, renowned throughout the world — each one in turn.

sanskrit: śalyaṃ pañcāśatā viddhvā kṛtavarmāṇam aṣṭabhiḥ kṛpasya saśaraṃ cāpaṃ madhye ciccheda bhārata athainaṃ chinnadhanvānaṃ punar vivyādha pañcabhiḥ
english: Having pierced Śalya with fifty shafts and Kṛtavarman with eight, he cut through the middle of Kṛpa's bow together with its arrow, O Bhārata; and when his bow was broken, he pierced him again with five.

sanskrit: vindānuvindau ca tathā tribhis tribhir atāḍayat durmarṣaṇaṃ ca viṃśatyā citrasenaṃ ca pañcabhiḥ
english: And he struck Vinda and Anuvinda with three arrows each, Durmarṣaṇa with twenty, and Citrasena with five.

sanskrit: vikarṇaṃ daśabhir bāṇaiḥ pañcabhiś ca jayadratham viddhvā bhīmo 'nadad dhṛṣṭaḥ saindhavaṃ ca punas tribhiḥ
english: Having pierced Vikarṇa with ten arrows and Jayadratha with five, Bhīma roared in delight, and struck the lord of the Sindhus once more with three.

sanskrit: athānyad dhanur ādāya gautamo rathināṃ varaḥ bhīmaṃ vivyādha saṃrabdho daśabhir niśitaiḥ śaraiḥ
english: Then, taking up another bow, the descendant of Gautama, foremost of car-warriors, pierced Bhīma in his fury with ten sharpened arrows.

sanskrit: sa viddho bahubhir bāṇais tottrair iva mahādvipaḥ tataḥ kruddho mahābāhur bhīmasenaḥ pratāpavān gautamaṃ tāḍayām āsa śarair bahubhir āhave
english: Pierced by many arrows like a great elephant by goads, the mighty-armed and valorous Bhīmasena, enraged, then struck the descendant of Gautama with a host of shafts in the fray.

sanskrit: saindhavasya tathāśvāṃś ca sārathiṃ ca tribhiḥ śaraiḥ prāhiṇon mṛtyulokāya kālāntakasamadyutiḥ
english: Then, with a splendor like that of Time the ender, he dispatched the steeds and the charioteer of the Sindhu lord to the realm of death with three arrows.

sanskrit: hatāśvāt tu rathāt tūrṇam avaplutya mahārathaḥ śarāṃś cikṣepa niśitān bhīmasenasya saṃyuge
english: Swiftly leaping down from his car whose horses were slain, that great car-warrior hurled sharp arrows at Bhīmasena in the battle.

sanskrit: tasya bhīmo dhanurmadhye dvābhyāṃ ciccheda bhārata bhallābhyāṃ bharataśreṣṭha saindhavasya mahātmanaḥ
english: With two broad-headed shafts, O best of the Bhāratas, Bhīma cut through the middle of the bow of that high-souled lord of the Sindhus.

sanskrit: sa cchinnadhanvā viratho hatāśvo hatasārathiḥ citrasenarathaṃ rājann āruroha tvarānvitaḥ
english: His bow severed, his car undone, his horses and charioteer slain, he climbed in haste, O king, onto the chariot of Citrasena.

sanskrit: atyadbhutaṃ raṇe karma kṛtavāṃs tatra pāṇḍavaḥ mahārathāñ śarair viddhvā vārayitvā mahārathaḥ virathaṃ saindhavaṃ cakre sarvalokasya paśyataḥ
english: A most wondrous deed the son of Pāṇḍu wrought there in the battle: that great car-warrior, having pierced and held off the mighty car-warriors with his arrows, stripped the Sindhu lord of his chariot before the eyes of all the world.

sanskrit: nātīva mamṛṣe śalyo bhīmasenasya vikramam sa saṃdhāya śarāṃs tīkṣṇān karmāraparimārjitān bhīmaṃ vivyādha saptatyā tiṣṭha tiṣṭheti cābravīt
english: Śalya could ill brook the prowess of Bhīmasena. Fitting to his bow sharp arrows burnished by the smith, he pierced Bhīma with seventy of them, crying, "Stand! Stand!"

sanskrit: kṛpaś ca kṛtavarmā ca bhagadattaś ca māriṣa vindānuvindāv āvantyau citrasenaś ca saṃyuge
english: And Kṛpa, Kṛtavarman, and Bhagadatta, O venerable one, Vinda and Anuvinda of Avanti, and Citrasena in the battle,

sanskrit: durmarṣaṇo vikarṇaś ca sindhurājaś ca vīryavān bhīmaṃ te vivyadhus tūrṇaṃ śalyahetor ariṃdamāḥ
english: Durmarṣaṇa and Vikarṇa, and the valiant king of the Sindhus — those tamers of foes swiftly pierced Bhīma for Śalya's sake.

sanskrit: sa tu tān prativivyādha pañcabhiḥ pañcabhiḥ śaraiḥ śalyaṃ vivyādha saptatyā punaś ca daśabhiḥ śaraiḥ
english: But he pierced them in return with five arrows each, and pierced Śalya with seventy, and again with ten shafts.

sanskrit: taṃ śalyo navabhir viddhvā punar vivyādha pañcabhiḥ sārathiṃ cāsya bhallena gāḍhaṃ vivyādha marmaṇi
english: Śalya, having pierced him with nine, pierced him again with five, and struck his charioteer deep in a vital part with a broad-headed shaft.

sanskrit: viśokaṃ vīkṣya nirbhinnaṃ bhīmasenaḥ pratāpavān madrarājaṃ tribhir bāṇair bāhvor urasi cārpayat
english: Seeing Viśoka pierced through, the valorous Bhīmasena planted three arrows in the arms and breast of the king of the Madras.

sanskrit: tathetarān maheṣvāsāṃs tribhis tribhir ajihmagaiḥ tāḍayām āsa samare siṃhavac ca nanāda ca
english: And the other great archers he struck, each with three straight-flying shafts, in the battle, and roared like a lion.

sanskrit: te hi yattā maheṣvāsāḥ pāṇḍavaṃ yuddhadurmadam tribhis tribhir akuṇṭhāgrair bhṛśaṃ marmasv atāḍayan
english: Those great archers, striving hard, struck the son of Pāṇḍu, intoxicated with battle, fiercely in his vital parts, each with three keen-pointed shafts.

sanskrit: so 'tividdho maheṣvāso bhīmaseno na vivyathe parvato vāridhārābhir varṣamāṇair ivāmbudaiḥ
english: Yet though sorely pierced, the great archer Bhīmasena did not waver — like a mountain under the streaming torrents of raining clouds.

sanskrit: śalyaṃ ca navabhir bāṇair bhṛśaṃ viddhvā mahāyaśāḥ prāgjyotiṣaṃ śatenājau rājan vivyādha vai dṛḍham
english: And having fiercely pierced Śalya with nine arrows, the greatly renowned one pierced the lord of Prāgjyotiṣa firmly in battle with a hundred, O king.

sanskrit: tatas tu saśaraṃ cāpaṃ sātvatasya mahātmanaḥ kṣurapreṇa sutīkṣṇena ciccheda kṛtahastavat
english: Then with a very sharp razor-edged shaft he cut, with the skill of a deft hand, the bow of the high-souled Sātvata together with its arrow.

sanskrit: athānyad dhanur ādāya kṛtavarmā vṛkodaram ājaghāna bhruvor madhye nārācena paraṃtapa
english: Then, taking up another bow, Kṛtavarman struck Vṛkodara between the brows with an iron shaft, O scorcher of foes.

sanskrit: bhīmas tu samare viddhvā śalyaṃ navabhir āyasaiḥ bhagadattaṃ tribhiś caiva kṛtavarmāṇam aṣṭabhiḥ
english: But Bhīma in the battle, having pierced Śalya with nine iron shafts, Bhagadatta with three and Kṛtavarman with eight,

sanskrit: dvābhyāṃ dvābhyāṃ ca vivyādha gautamaprabhṛtīn rathān te tu taṃ samare rājan vivyadhur niśitaiḥ śaraiḥ
english: pierced the car-warriors led by Gautama with two arrows each; and they in turn, O king, pierced him in the battle with sharpened shafts.

sanskrit: sa tathā pīḍyamāno 'pi sarvatas tair mahārathaiḥ matvā tṛṇena tāṃs tulyān vicacāra gatavyathaḥ
english: Though thus afflicted on every side by those great car-warriors, he, accounting them no more than blades of grass, ranged about free of distress.

sanskrit: te cāpi rathināṃ śreṣṭhā bhīmāya niśitāñ śarān preṣayām āsur avyagrāḥ śataśo 'tha sahasraśaḥ
english: And those foremost of car-warriors, unflustered, sent forth at Bhīma their sharpened arrows by the hundreds and the thousands.

sanskrit: tasya śaktiṃ mahāvegāṃ bhagadatto mahārathaḥ cikṣepa samare vīraḥ svarṇadaṇḍāṃ mahādhanām
english: At him the heroic great car-warrior Bhagadatta hurled in the battle a javelin of great speed, gold-shafted and of great worth.

sanskrit: tomaraṃ saindhavo rājā paṭṭiśaṃ ca mahābhujaḥ śataghnīṃ ca kṛpo rājañ śaraṃ śalyaś ca saṃyuge
english: The Sindhu king cast a lance, and the mighty-armed one a barbed spear; Kṛpa hurled a śataghnī, O king, and Śalya an arrow in the fight.

sanskrit: athetare maheṣvāsāḥ pañca pañca śilīmukhān bhīmasenaṃ samuddiśya preṣayām āsur ojasā
english: Then the other great archers, aiming at Bhīmasena, sent forth five arrows each with all their might.

sanskrit: tomaraṃ sa dvidhā cakre kṣurapreṇānilātmajaḥ paṭṭiśaṃ ca tribhir bāṇaiś ciccheda tilakāṇḍavat
english: The son of the Wind cleft the lance in two with a razor-edged shaft, and cut the barbed spear with three arrows as if it were a sesame stalk.

sanskrit: sa bibheda śataghnīṃ ca navabhiḥ kaṅkapatribhiḥ madrarājaprayuktaṃ ca śaraṃ chittvā mahābalaḥ
english: And the mighty one shattered the śataghnī with nine heron-feathered shafts, and cut down the arrow loosed by the king of the Madras.

sanskrit: śaktiṃ ciccheda sahasā bhagadatteritāṃ raṇe tathetarāñ śarān ghorāñ śaraiḥ saṃnataparvabhiḥ
english: Swiftly he cut down the javelin hurled by Bhagadatta in the battle, and likewise the other dreadful shafts with his own well-jointed arrows.

sanskrit: bhīmaseno raṇaślāghī tridhaikaikaṃ samācchinat tāṃś ca sarvān maheṣvāsāṃs tribhis tribhir atāḍayat
english: Bhīmasena, glorying in war, clove each one of them into three, and struck all those great archers, each with three shafts.

sanskrit: tato dhanaṃjayas tatra vartamāne mahāraṇe jagāma sa rathenājau bhīmaṃ dṛṣṭvā mahāratham nighnantaṃ samare śatrūn yodhayānaṃ ca sāyakaiḥ
english: Then, while that great battle raged, Dhanaṃjaya advanced there in his car, beholding the great car-warrior Bhīma — striking down the foes in the fray and contending with his arrows.

sanskrit: tau tu tatra mahātmānau sametau vīkṣya pāṇḍavau nāśaśaṃsur jayaṃ tatra tāvakāḥ puruṣarṣabha
english: And beholding those two high-souled sons of Pāṇḍu joined together there, your men no longer hoped for victory, O bull among men.

sanskrit: athārjuno raṇe bhīṣmaṃ yodhayan vai mahāratham bhīṣmasya nidhanākāṅkṣī puraskṛtya śikhaṇḍinam
english: Then Arjuna, contending in the battle with the great car-warrior Bhīṣma and longing for Bhīṣma's death, placed Śikhaṇḍin before him,

sanskrit: āsasāda raṇe yodhāṃs tāvakān daśa bhārata ye sma bhīmaṃ raṇe rājan yodhayanto vyavasthitāḥ bībhatsus tān athāvidhyad bhīmasya priyakāmyayā
english: and fell upon those ten warriors of your side in the battle, O Bhārata, who stood there fighting against Bhīma, O king; and Bībhatsu pierced them, wishing to do Bhīma a kindness.

sanskrit: tato duryodhano rājā suśarmāṇam acodayat arjunasya vadhārthāya bhīmasenasya cobhayoḥ
english: Then king Duryodhana urged on Suśarman for the slaying of both Arjuna and Bhīmasena.

sanskrit: suśarman gaccha śīghraṃ tvaṃ balaughaiḥ parivāritaḥ jahi pāṇḍusutāv etau dhanaṃjayavṛkodarau
english: "Suśarman, go swiftly, encompassed by your floods of troops, and slay these two sons of Pāṇḍu, Dhanaṃjaya and Vṛkodara."

sanskrit: tac chrutvā śāsanaṃ tasya trigartaḥ prasthalādhipaḥ abhidrutya raṇe bhīmam arjunaṃ caiva dhanvinau
english: Hearing that command of his, the Trigarta lord of Prasthala rushed in the battle upon Bhīma and Arjuna, those two bowmen,

sanskrit: rathair anekasāhasraiḥ parivavre samantataḥ tataḥ pravavṛte yuddham arjunasya paraiḥ saha
english: and surrounded them on every side with chariots by the many thousands; thereupon the battle began between Arjuna and his foes.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca arjunas tu raṇe śalyaṃ yatamānaṃ mahāratham chādayām āsa samare śaraiḥ saṃnataparvabhiḥ
english: Saṃjaya said: But Arjuna in the battle covered the striving great car-warrior Śalya with his well-jointed arrows.

sanskrit: suśarmāṇaṃ kṛpaṃ caiva tribhis tribhir avidhyata prāgjyotiṣaṃ ca samare saindhavaṃ ca jayadratham
english: He pierced Suśarman and Kṛpa with three arrows each, and the lord of Prāgjyotiṣa in the battle, and Jayadratha of the Sindhus,

sanskrit: citrasenaṃ vikarṇaṃ ca kṛtavarmāṇam eva ca durmarṣaṇaṃ ca rājendra āvantyau ca mahārathau
english: and Citrasena and Vikarṇa and Kṛtavarman too, and Durmarṣaṇa, O lord of kings, and the two great car-warriors of Avanti —

sanskrit: ekaikaṃ tribhir ānarchat kaṅkabarhiṇavājitaiḥ śarair atiratho yuddhe pīḍayan vāhinīṃ tava
english: each one he struck with three arrows fledged with the feathers of heron and peacock, that surpassing car-warrior, harrying your host in the fight.

sanskrit: jayadratho raṇe pārthaṃ bhittvā bhārata sāyakaiḥ bhīmaṃ vivyādha tarasā citrasenarathe sthitaḥ
english: Jayadratha in the battle, having pierced Pārtha with arrows, O Bhārata, swiftly pierced Bhīma, standing upon the chariot of Citrasena.

sanskrit: śalyaś ca samare jiṣṇuṃ kṛpaś ca rathināṃ varaḥ vivyadhāte mahābāhuṃ bahudhā marmabhedibhiḥ
english: And Śalya in the battle, and Kṛpa the foremost of car-warriors, pierced the mighty-armed Jiṣṇu again and again with vital-piercing shafts.

sanskrit: citrasenādayaś caiva putrās tava viśāṃ pate pañcabhiḥ pañcabhis tūrṇaṃ saṃyuge niśitaiḥ śaraiḥ ājaghnur arjunaṃ saṃkhye bhīmasenaṃ ca māriṣa
english: And your sons led by Citrasena, O lord of peoples, swiftly in the battle struck Arjuna in the fray and Bhīmasena, O venerable one, each with five sharpened arrows.

sanskrit: tau tatra rathināṃ śreṣṭhau kaunteyau bharatarṣabhau apīḍayetāṃ samare trigartānāṃ mahad balam
english: Those two foremost of car-warriors, the sons of Kuntī, bulls among the Bhāratas, harried in the battle the great force of the Trigartas.

sanskrit: suśarmāpi raṇe pārthaṃ viddhvā bahubhir āyasaiḥ nanāda balavan nādaṃ nādayan vai nabhastalam
english: Suśarman too in the battle, having pierced Pārtha with many iron shafts, roared a mighty roar that made the very vault of heaven resound.

sanskrit: anye ca rathinaḥ śūrā bhīmasenadhanaṃjayau vivyadhur niśitair bāṇai rukmapuṅkhair ajihmagaiḥ
english: And other valiant car-warriors pierced Bhīmasena and Dhanaṃjaya with sharpened arrows, gold-nocked and straight-flying.

sanskrit: teṣāṃ tu rathināṃ madhye kaunteyau rathināṃ varau krīḍamānau rathodārau citrarūpau vyarocatām āmiṣepsū gavāṃ madhye siṃhāv iva balotkaṭau
english: In the midst of those car-warriors the two sons of Kuntī, foremost of car-warriors, sporting in their splendid chariots and wondrous in form, shone resplendent — like two lions fierce in strength, greedy for prey, amid a herd of cattle.

sanskrit: chittvā dhanūṃṣi vīrāṇāṃ śarāṃś ca bahudhā raṇe pātayām āsatur vīrau śirāṃsi śataśo nṛṇām
english: Cutting asunder the bows of the heroes and their arrows in many ways in the battle, those two warriors struck down the heads of men by the hundreds.
